dwp_take: AMD just released Ross, an AI assistant specifically built to help engineers with embedded system design, optimization, and debugging work. This matters because digital workplace teams managing technical infrastructure and developer tools now have another AI option to evaluate for improving engineering productivity and reducing time spent on routine troubleshooting tasks. Honestly though, we've got so many AI assistants launching these days that the real question isn't whether Ross exists, it's whether your engineers will actually use it or just stick with whatever they already know.

After three decades watching Microsoft's versioning strategy, I can confirm this is basically them playing 4D chess while the rest of us are still figuring out checkers.

title: Snowflake urges companies to embrace the era of the agentic enterprise
excerpt: The pace of change is unrelenting, so doing nothing is no longer an option, the AI data firm told attendees at a recent event in London…
dwp_take: Snowflake is telling companies they need to get serious about AI agents handling enterprise tasks or risk getting left behind. This matters to digital workplace folks because autonomous agents are going to fundamentally change how work gets done, who does it, and what skills actually matter in an office. Here's the thing though: every vendor says "embrace change or die," and most companies are still struggling with basic collaboration tools, so maybe pump the brakes on the existential dread and focus on getting your fundamentals right first.

title: NetApp Insight 2026: Can Novus and Keystone break the AI bottlenecks?
excerpt: We're back in Vegas as Ross Kelly talks us through all the news from NetApp Insight 2026
dwp_take: NetApp announced Novus and Keystone at their Vegas conference, positioning both as solutions to tackle AI infrastructure bottlenecks that are currently slowing down enterprise deployments. This matters because data storage and management remain the unsexy but critical foundation that every AI initiative actually needs to function, and most organizations are still struggling with this unglamorous reality. Look, if your AI strategy falls apart because your storage can't keep up, all those fancy LLM conversations don't mean much, so NetApp is at least tackling the real problem instead of just selling you another chatbot.
